# pengdows.efcore.conformance

> Black-box conformance tests for relational providers of Entity Framework Core 10.

## Purpose

This repository tests externally observable behavior through documented EF Core public APIs. The provider is configured through an adapter, operations run through `DbContext`, LINQ, and EF Core relational APIs, and results are asserted through fresh contexts or documented public state.

## Boundary

- Do not inspect generated SQL, EF provider services, EF internals, or provider implementation types in shared tests.
- Keep provider setup and database provisioning in `IProviderAdapter` implementations.
- Capabilities declare applicability only. They never alter expected values or assertions.
- Strict runs require a supported or unsupported declaration for every feature in `ProviderCapabilities.KnownFeatures`.
- ADO.NET `DataTypes` metadata is the preferred native type inventory. Mark catalog evidence independent only when it is independent of the EF model. Types read from test-created tables are `SELF_DERIVED` and excluded from coverage totals.
- Run the same test assembly against one provider per process. Compare report JSON with the runner's `--compare` command.

## Project map

- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Contracts/`: adapter contracts, capabilities, type discovery, and outcomes.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner/`: adapter loading, test execution, JSON/JUnit reports, type discovery, and cross-provider comparison.
- `src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Inventory/`: reflection-generated EF Core public API inventory.
- `tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/`: shared EF Core 10 relational behavioral tests.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/`: Microsoft provider reference adapter; included in the standalone solution.
- `adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.PengdowsSqlite/`: pengdows adapter; depends on the separate pengdows ADO.NET repository and is intentionally outside the solution build.
- `manifests/`: EF Core 10 contract and generated API inventory.

## Build and run

```sh
dotnet build pengdows.efcore.conformance.slnx
export PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING='Data Source=/tmp/efcore-reference.db'
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --run \
  tests/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational/pengdows.efcore.conformance.EF10.Relational.csproj \
  "$PWD/adapters/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite/bin/Debug/net10.0/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.dll" \
  pengdows.efcore.conformance.Adapter.MicrosoftSqlite.MicrosoftSqliteAdapter /tmp/efcore-reference-report
```

Run the same test assembly for another provider with a separate disposable database and report directory. Compare results:

```sh
dotnet run --project src/pengdows.efcore.conformance.Runner -- --compare \
  /tmp/candidate-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/efcore-reference-report/conformance-results.json \
  /tmp/provider-comparison.json
```

Append `--cleanup-database` to `--run` only when the configured database is dedicated and disposable. The runner then calls the adapter cleanup hook after writing test results.

## Provider configuration

The sibling ADO.NET conformance project uses `providers/*.json` profiles to describe driver, target, connection string, environment, dialect, and type inventory. The EF Core harness borrows declarative per-provider profiles for adapter selection and connection strings: `profiles/*.json` names a compiled adapter assembly/type and a connection string template with `${ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE}` placeholders. Run one with `--run-profile <profile.json> <test-project> <report-directory> [--cleanup-database]`. Adapter assembly paths are relative to the profile file unless absolute.

EF profiles deliberately leave EF provider configuration, capabilities, database initialization, and cleanup in `IProviderAdapter`. A profile cannot change expectations or assertions. Profiles do not provision containers or remote databases; infrastructure setup remains external. The old direct `--run` form and `PENGDOWS_EFCORE_CONFORMANCE_CONNECTION_STRING` are still supported.

## Current status

- EF Core baseline: 10.0.14 on `net10.0`.
- The public API inventory is generated from the Core, Abstractions, and Relational assemblies. Disposition rules in `manifests/efcore-10.json` attach rationales to EF-owned and provider-service surfaces; tests override those rules. Current counts: 643 overload entries in tested API families, 31 uncovered member families, 35 entries awaiting classification, 3,523 EF-owned entries, and 8,347 provider-service or model-configuration entries marked not directly applicable.
- Latest full runs execute 324 cases per provider: 306 pass on pengdows SQLite, 311 on Microsoft SQLite, and 311 on Pomelo MySQL; 5 decimal fidelity cases fail only on pengdows SQLite; 5 cases fail on all three. The two ambient-transaction and two Least/Greatest function cases plus two SQLite index-rename/check-constraint migration cases and the SQLite index-metadata and schema-comment cases are unsupported by both SQLite adapters; the function cases are also unsupported by Pomelo. The public `CreateDbCommand` query execution case, all sync and async parameterized collection mode cases, explicit sync and async `EF.MultipleParameters(collection)` calls, and both `EF.Functions.Random()` behavior cases pass on both providers. Shared failures are async negative `ElementAt`, both `RightJoin` unmatched-row cases, and both TPT affected-entry-count cases. Shared failures are not automatically attributed to EF Core. Both providers pass keyless `[Keyless]` entity materialization through parameterized `FromSqlInterpolated` in sync and async paths, shadow-property filtering through `EF.Property` and predicate evaluation through `EF.Constant`/`EF.Parameter`/`EF.MultipleParameters`, and escaped wildcard matching through `EF.Functions.Like` and parameterized `EF.CompileQuery`/`EF.CompileAsyncQuery` on sync/async paths, boundary round-trips for CLR date, time, boolean, binary, and converted enum values, sync/async store-generated integer keys, pre-canceled async query and SaveChanges operations, sync/async SaveChanges behavior with automatic change detection disabled, context-wide sync/async `QueryTrackingBehavior`, sync/async snapshot and notification change-tracking strategies, `SaveChanges(false)` state retention followed by `AcceptAllChanges`, and changes with snapshot detection disabled, sync/async `WarningBehavior` handling for `Log`, `Ignore`, and `Throw`, sync/async materialization under all supported `PropertyAccessMode` values, `TrackGraph`, deferred `CascadeChanges`, sync/async nested complex-value updates, sync/async optimistic concurrency conflict recovery, sync/async DI-created `IDbContextFactory` contexts and scoped `AddDbContext` contexts, savepoint release and transaction interface checks, database facade provider/transaction/savepoint configuration cases, `DatabaseFacade` commit/rollback methods, `PropertyValues.SetValues` and snapshot helpers, direct `EntityEntry.DetectChanges`, `DbContext` success and failure events, `DbSet` convenience and async enumerator cases, `AsTracking` overrides, sync and async query `Load`, context disposal and owned-connection closure, `IgnoreAutoIncludes`, async `ForEachAsync` and array/set/dictionary materializers, direct `DbContext` add/attach/update/remove and range operations, current-database-value checks for tracked entities, explicit collection/reference loading, migration discovery/application including table rename, raw SQL migration operations, and rollback/reapply, migration-created foreign key, unique constraint, and check constraint enforcement, keyless `[Keyless]` raw SQL materialization, sync/async `Cascade`, `SetNull`, `ClientCascade`, `ClientSetNull`, `NoAction`, and `ClientNoAction` delete behavior, generic and non-generic `[EntityTypeConfiguration]` attributes and `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` model mappings and `[Owned]` attribute-driven model mappings, getter-only property persistence through `[BackingField]`, filtered unique index behavior controlled by the declared `filtered-indexes` capability, nested owned-to-JSON persistence and property queries controlled by `json-mapping`, unique index enforcement from `[Index]`, built-in function translation from `[DbFunction]`, nullable function result preservation on sync and async paths, precision attribute value fidelity, database deletion/recreation checks, synchronous and asynchronous `UseSeeding`/`UseAsyncSeeding` hooks, and pending-model-change checks, external ADO.NET transaction cases, external connection replacement, `CreateDbCommand` result execution, scalar `SqlQueryRaw<T>` cases, generic `DbContext.Find`/`FindAsync` cases, database facade configuration cases, warning configuration, and `ExecuteSql`/`ExecuteSqlAsync` command cases.
- Added optional Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 adapter and profile. The 324-case run passes 311, fails 5 (the shared async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async `RightJoin`, and sync/async TPT count cases), and reports 8 explicit unsupported outcomes: filtered indexes, JSON mapping, primitive collections, and `Least`/`Greatest` translation. SQLite declares ambient `System.Transactions` unsupported, while MySQL passes the sync and async enlistment cases.
- MySQL Connector independently advertises `DataTypes`: 51 metadata rows, 41 distinct names, zero unresolved CLR names, and no discovery diagnostics. The 51 rows represent 49 mapping variants; reports retain CLR type, provider type ID, and declaration format rather than collapsing them by native name. Current declarations cover 4 variants, partially cover 1, leave 44 uncovered, and do not observe 8 declared test names. Native-type behavioral tests are still hand-declared rather than generated from discovery.
- SQLite ADO.NET providers do not advertise `DataTypes`. Supplemental types discovered from test-created schema are self-derived; independent native type coverage is not currently established for SQLite.
- Public type declarations, compiler-generated enum backing fields, and inherited `System.Object` overrides carry explicit non-applicability rationales because they are inventory nodes or EF-owned object behavior rather than provider operations. The test suite is a growing conformance slice, not yet complete coverage of every applicable EF Core public API. Consult `README.md`, `manifests/efcore-10.json`, and `manifests/efcore-10-api-inventory.json` for disposition rules, current counts, rationales, and uncovered members.


## Unfinished work

Inventory dimensions overlap: unclassified entries can belong to uncovered member families and must not be summed.

1. Classify all 35 `unclassified` entries with a reason or behavioral test. The largest cluster is `MigrationBuilder` (27 entries), followed by relational builder extensions and capability enums.
2. Add behavioral contracts for the 31 uncovered public API member families. Cover each observable provider responsibility, including separate sync and async paths where both APIs exist. An inventory link alone does not cover all overloads or scenarios.
3. Triage the five pengdows-only decimal fidelity failures. Investigate the five failures reproduced by both SQLite providers (async negative `ElementAt`, sync/async unmatched `RightJoin`, sync/async TPT save counts) against documented contracts and additional providers. Reproduction on the reference provider is evidence, not proof of an EF Core defect.
4. Complete native-type fidelity. MySQL supplies an independent ADO.NET `DataTypes` inventory, but only 4 names currently have behavioral coverage and no discovery-driven round-trip tests exist. Compare metadata with the server catalog, record discrepancies, and exercise insertion, retrieval, parameterization, updates, and applicable queries for each discovered type.
5. Expand beyond the first Pomelo/MySQL 8.4 run to additional relational providers and server versions, keeping shared expectations provider-independent and capability declarations explicit.
6. Add a separate EF Core 11 target after its release contract is established; generate its inventory from its actual assemblies and add version-specific tests for changed or new behavior.

EF Core 10 completion requires zero unclassified entries, behavioral or justified disposition for each applicable public API family, sync/async coverage where both APIs exist, independently discovered native-type coverage, triaged failures, and reports that distinguish pass, fail, unsupported, infrastructure error, and uncovered work. The current 324-case three-provider comparison is an initial slice, not completion.
